policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: The article before θεός is not rendered in English: ASV 'hath her hope set on God' reads identically for θεὸν and τὸν θεὸν, and no note is mapped here.
ASV 'and specially his own household' shows nothing that would distinguish μάλιστα from μάλιστα τῶν; the genitive article leaves no English trace.
Active προνοεῖ and middle προνοεῖται carry the same sense with the same subject; ASV 'if any provideth not for his own' renders either, and no note is mapped here.
ASV limits the condition to a woman — 'If any woman that believeth hath widows' — with no 'believing man or' answering RP's added πιστὸς ἤ, so the shorter τις stands.
ASV 'let her relieve them' keeps the believing woman as the one who relieves, which both the active ἐπαρκείτω and the middle ἐπαρκείσθω permit; the English does not expose the voice.
ASV opens 'Them that sin reprove' with no connective, but an unrendered δέ is unremarkable in ASV; the absence of 'but'/'and' does not settle whether δέ stood in the text.

ASV reads 'and Christ Jesus' — the two-name order without κυρίου, where RP's κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ would give 'the Lord Jesus Christ'. The mapped note is alternative_rendering (on 'prejudice') and bears on wording only.

ASV 'thy stomach's sake and thine often infirmities' has a σου in the base text attached to ἀσθενείας, and English idiom requires a possessive with 'stomach' regardless; 'thy' therefore does not require the added σου.
The mapped note gives the Greek as 'the works that are good are evident' — the articular attributive ἔργα τὰ καλά — rather than the plain attributive καλὰ ἔργα of RP.
The copula in ASV 'there are good works that are evident' (and in the note's gloss 'are evident') is required by English whether or not ἐστίν stood in the Greek.
